Use ONLY TOP LEFT panel of reference 1. Frontal wide establishing view of the enormous ruined industrial hall, centered vanishing point and tiny distant red target beacon. Keep the original flooded pits and broken narrow path. Lighting change REQUIRED: almost all of the room falls into near-black. A soft-edged localized pool of light from an INVISIBLE source behind camera catches just part of the nearest broken walkway and a small farther pier; surrounding darkness conceals most surfaces. This is one still instant of slowly moving exploratory illumination, not a visible handheld flashlight or searchlight fixture. Retain readable hints of scale. No evenly lit panoramic beauty shot. The next shot looks down at floor texture; keep illuminated foreground as the visual bridge.

Reference 1 is the ONLY composition and terrain master. Output ONE standalone 16:9 shot, not a contact sheet. Preserve exact camera orientation, lens perspective, slab silhouettes, gaps, rubble distribution, water locations, pipes, columns and destination position. No rebuilding, widening, straightening, smoothing or simplifying the route. Do not import background or camera geometry from any other reference. No additional props, hands, flashlight objects, people, text or HUD.

MATERIAL AND TONAL CORRECTION IS ESSENTIAL, not a subtle optional finish. The scene reference is approved ONLY for geometry and composition, NOT its current glossy HDR rendering. Replace that rendering throughout the ENTIRE ENVIRONMENT, not just the robot.
Photographic low-key exposure with restrained contrast and soft highlight roll-off. Reduce hard white sparkles across foreground concrete, pipework and water. Preserve surrounding water and a few subdued, broken reflections; do not dry the flooded space. Concrete is predominantly rough, porous and diffuse, with irregular dusty dry patches, damp dark patches and isolated small puddles, not an evenly lacquered glossy surface. Rust is dull and coarse, not polished copper. Rubber feet absorb light; painted gray robot shell has broad soft satin reflections, never chrome or plastic glare.
Remove crunchy local contrast, clarity enhancement, edge halos, excessive sharpening, saturated orange rust and blue/orange grading. Shadows remain dark yet contain modest natural texture. Do not merely darken the whole picture, gray-wash it, blur detail or add haze to hide the problem. Keep original light direction and practical beacon position, but soften reflected highlights and tonal transitions visibly. Natural imperfect surface variation, muted neutral color, no showroom polish.
